decisions.reason: As a newly launched plugin that is close to the firm’s core shop-customization offer, it is likely to be retained while management gathers more evidence because no clear shortfall is yet visible and the resource commitment is modest.
The ERP interface plugin fits the firm’s strategic move toward broader multichannel support and should be kept unless results clearly disappoint, which is not indicated at this early stage.

Although it is near the core business and still very new, the presence of several similar price-comparison tracking plugins raises the aspiration threshold and makes later pruning possible, but not yet the most likely choice.

Management would probably continue this close-to-core tracking plugin for another year because early uncertainty and some organizational slack favor learning before exit, even though overlap with similar products increases risk.

This plugin is also likely to be given more time because it builds on existing capabilities, but its redundancy within a cluster of similar tracking tools makes it one of the more vulnerable products if performance proves weak.

The net price reporting plugin complements the firm’s established e-commerce optimization work, so a behavioral-theory management would usually keep it on the market while evaluating uptake against emerging aspirations.
